description: REQ-010's entire safety argument rests on the claim that the clip's filename-based ID is 'already unique per clip by construction, no new ID-generation logic needed.' This is FALSE against the real code the spec itself cites as ground truth. producer.sh:60 derives clip_id purely from the SOURCE VIDEO URL (`sed 's#.*v=##; s#[^A-Za-z0-9_-]##g' | head -c 16`), NOT from anything unique to the specific 9:16 cut or the processing run. producer.sh's own default source-selection (lines 30-34, no --url given) picks the SINGLE MOST RECENT video from a fixed channel (`yt_dlp --flat-playlist --playlist-end 1 ... @theDiaryOfACEO/videos`) with ZERO history/dedup check against already-processed URLs. producer.sh's own file header states it is 'run as a DAILY producer cron' (line 5). Any day the channel does not publish a new video before the next cron fire -- a routine occurrence, not a rare edge case -- producer.sh will deterministically re-derive the IDENTICAL clip_id as a prior run. It will also collide on every manual `producer.sh --url <same-url>` retry. Concretely: if an OLDER clip with clip_id X is sitting unresolved in $CLIP_PENDING_VERIFY (its sidecar token = '#cX'), and a NEWER, content-different clip is produced from the same recurring source video (same clip_id X, therefore the IDENTICAL token '#cX' per REQ-010's own derivation formula) and successfully posted via the direct live path, self-heal for the OLDER clip will compute new_hrefs against its own before_hrefs, find the NEWER clip's freshly-posted href in that diff, navigate to it, find token '#cX' present in its innerText (because the NEWER clip's caption ALSO carries token '#cX'), and misattribute the NEWER clip's real post_url to the OLDER, possibly-never-actually-published clip -- moving it to $CLIP_POSTED with a post_url that belongs to a different clip entirely. This is the exact class of misattribution bug REQ-010 was introduced specifically to eliminate (iteration-10 FIND-025), now reintroduced through clip_id reuse instead of hook-text reuse. The spec's blanket claim '...there is no meaningful residual token-collision risk (unlike the withdrawn caption-prose approach): tokens are derived 1:1 from each clip's own unique source-URL-based ID' (behavioral-spec.md REQ-008 step 6, final paragraph) is not merely optimistic -- it is empirically false against producer.sh's real default behavior, and the spec's 'In scope'/'Out of scope' sections and REQ-010 itself never enumerate or address this edge case at all. Also note a related, independent data-loss risk: producer.sh:61-62 (`DEST="$QUEUE/${ID}_EN.mp4"; cp "$WORK/EN.mp4" "$DEST"`) will SILENTLY OVERWRITE an existing not-yet-posted queued clip of the same ID, which further confirms clip_id was never designed as a collision-proof identity key.

evidence.snippet:
VID=$("$PY" -m yt_dlp --flat-playlist --playlist-end 1 --print "%(id)s" "https://www.youtube.com/@theDiaryOfACEO/videos" ...)
...
ID=$(printf '%s' "$URL" | sed 's#.*v=##; s#[^A-Za-z0-9_-]##g' | head -c 16)
DEST="$QUEUE/${ID}_EN.mp4"
